cartes: Battle of the Boyne: James II is beaten by William of Orange
Great Irish Famine (potato blight 1845-1848): about 1 million dead, 2 million emigrants
Failed armed uprising of the Young Irelanders (tricolour flag)
Easter Rising: insurrection led by James Connolly and Patrick Pearse
Éamon de Valera is elected president of Sinn Féin
Irish War of Independence (IRA v. British forces)
Southern Ireland becomes the "Republic of Ireland" / Éire
War of Independence: the island is partitioned into two entities
Official birth of Northern Ireland (6 counties)
Easter Rising (Connolly and Pearse), violently repressed by the British: 6 days, about 370 dead, 15 leaders hanged
Anglo-Irish Treaty: Irish Free State (26 counties) and Northern Ireland (6 counties)
Irish Civil War (pro-treaty victory, partition accepted)
Northern Irish Parliament election: 40 unionists, 6 nationalists, 6 Sinn Féin
Special Powers Act (extended powers for the RUC police)
NICRA (Northern Ireland Civil Rights Association) is created
Bloody Sunday in Derry: 13 protesters killed by British paratroopers (14 on the Cameron slide)
Widgery Report on Bloody Sunday (finds no fault in the soldiers)
Stormont suspended, Direct Rule from London imposed
Start of the "dirty protest" by IRA prisoners in the H-Blocks
IRA prisoners' hunger strike at the Maze prison
Bobby Sands begins a hunger strike
Death of Bobby Sands (and 9 other hunger strikers)
Tony Blair announces a new inquiry (Saville) into Bloody Sunday
Saville Report published: the victims were unarmed civilians and the soldiers lied
David Cameron's official apology for Bloody Sunday
Power-sharing government in Northern Ireland: Ian Paisley (DUP) and Martin McGuinness (Sinn Féin)
Northern Irish First Minister Paul Givan (DUP) resigns
Historic Sinn Féin victory in Northern Ireland (27 seats to the DUP's 25); Michelle O'Neill becomes First Minister
Michelle O'Neill runs a campaign on cost of living and health rather than reunification
Northern Ireland census: 45.7% Catholic, 43.5% Protestant (first time in 101 years)
"Celtic alliance": Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland jointly demand a vote on dissolving the UK (Cardiff)
Simon Jenkins article in The Guardian on the Celtic alliance
